text:
yasmin: hey all, new hire here. trying to run the dev stack and my app fails to connect to Postgres with:

`psql: FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry for host "172.19.0.1", user "app", database "app_development", SSL off`

I haven't touched pg_hba.conf and the container says `Listening on 0.0.0.0:5432`. any hints?

cory: welcome! that error usually means Postgres is rejecting the connection based on pg_hba rules. Important distinction: connections from the host to the published port look like they come from the Docker VM/bridge IP (eg 172.19.0.1), not `localhost`. By default pg_hba might only allow local socket or 127.0.0.1.

yasmin: oh interesting. i tried connecting from my Windows host using `psql -h localhost -p 5433` after publish 5433:5432. should i add an entry to pg_hba.conf?

diego: two safer options before editing pg_hba: 1) if your app runs in another container, talk to `db:5432` (service name) — that's in-network and works with the default config. 2) if you must connect from the host, add a permissive dev-only entry to pg_hba.conf (or set `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust` for a throwaway dev container). Example pg_hba line: `host all all 172.16.0.0/12 md5` or `host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5` (last one is only OK in private dev).

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "Note: editing pg_hba.conf requires container restart (or use exec to reload)."

yasmin: i prefer not to loosen pg_hba. my app runs on the Windows host (not in WSL). if docker publish maps 5433 to 5432, why does Postgres see the host IP as 172.19.0.1 and not 127.0.0.1?

cory: (jumping in) When Docker Desktop (WSL2) publishes a port, the connection from Windows -> container goes through NAT and appears to Postgres as coming from the bridge network IP. The container sees the source IP inside the Docker network, not the Windows loopback. That's why pg_hba sees 172.x.

yasmin: got it. so simplest approach: add a specific pg_hba entry for that bridge range? any recommended pattern for onboarding docs?

diego: For onboarding we do: 1) recommend running app in-compose (service name) to avoid host networking issues; 2) if running on host, prefer `localhost` and published port but document that you may need to add a host entry in pg_hba for the Docker subnet (we include a sample dev pg_hba in the repo). Sample dev snippet we use (string in docs):
```
# dev-only: allow Docker bridge network
host all all 172.16.0.0/12 md5
# fallback for host connections
host all all 127.0.0.1/32 md5
```

yasmin: i also saw references to `host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5` vs `trust`. which is less bad?

cory: md5 (password) is fine for dev if you have a real password set. `trust` disables auth entirely — okay only for throwaway envs. We avoid `0.0.0.0/0` in shared networks though. Pin the cidr to the docker bridge if you can.

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "Reminder: if using mounted pg_hba.conf from host, watch out for CRLF/permissions on Windows mounts."

yasmin: thank you! made a tiny change to the repo to include `pg_hba.dev.conf` and updated compose to mount it for dev only. works now — migrations ran. i'll open a PR to add a short note about the Docker bridge IP behavior and the dev pg_hba sample.

diego: awesome, ping me on the PR and welcome aboard! :tada:
